name: Digital Forensics
description: Acquiring, preserving and analyzing digital evidence from disks, memory and logs in a forensically sound way.

resources.title: NIST SP 800-86: Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response
SANS Digital Forensics and Incident Response

questions.question: Following the order of volatility, which source should generally be collected first from a running system?
options: A full hard-disk image
Archived backup tapes
System memory (RAM)
Printed documentation
questions.explanation: RAM contents are lost when the system powers off or changes, so the most volatile evidence is captured before disks and backups.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a chain of custody record?
options: To document who handled the evidence, when, and what was done, demonstrating it was not tampered with
To list all the malware found on a device
To encrypt evidence so suspects cannot read it
To record the network topology of the organization
questions.explanation: Chain of custody tracks every transfer and action on evidence so its integrity and admissibility can be demonstrated.

questions.question: Why is a hardware or software write blocker used when acquiring a disk image?
options: To speed up the imaging process
To compress the image to save space
To decrypt encrypted volumes automatically
To prevent any writes to the source drive, so the original evidence is not modified
questions.explanation: Simply mounting a drive can change metadata. A write blocker allows reads only, preserving the original evidence.

questions.question: On an NTFS volume, which file-system structure holds a record for every file, including its timestamps and attributes?
options: pagefile.sys
$MFT (Master File Table)
hiberfil.sys
desktop.ini
questions.explanation: The Master File Table contains an entry per file with metadata such as $STANDARD_INFORMATION and $FILE_NAME timestamps.

questions.question: After acquiring a drive image, the SHA-256 hash of the source and the hash of the image do not match. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
options: The image is valid because hashes often differ slightly
SHA-256 is broken, so switch to MD5
The image cannot be shown to be an exact copy; investigate the cause and re-acquire before analysis
Delete the source drive to avoid confusion
questions.explanation: Matching hashes are how examiners prove the image is bit-for-bit identical. A mismatch means integrity is unproven, so the acquisition must be investigated and repeated.

questions.question: What is the Volatility framework primarily used for?
options: Carving deleted files from unallocated disk space
Capturing live network packets
Aggregating logs into a SIEM
Analyzing memory images for processes, network connections and injected code
questions.explanation: Volatility is an open-source memory forensics framework that extracts artifacts such as process lists, sockets and loaded modules from RAM dumps.

practical.title: Verify evidence integrity with a hash
practical.instructions: You have acquired a disk image named evidence.img in an authorized lab investigation. Write the command (Linux or Windows PowerShell) to compute its SHA-256 hash, then write 1-2 sentences explaining why you record this hash and when you would compute it again.
practical.expected_output: A command such as 'sha256sum evidence.img' or 'Get-FileHash evidence.img -Algorithm SHA256', plus an explanation that the hash proves integrity (the image is unaltered) and is recomputed later/before analysis or in court to verify it matches, supporting chain of custody.

rubric.hint: Use sha256sum (Linux), Get-FileHash (PowerShell), shasum -a 256 or certutil -hashfile ... SHA256.
The hash proves the evidence has not been altered and supports chain of custody.
Recompute and compare the hash later (e.g. before analysis or presentation) to confirm it still matches.

tasks.title: Learn the forensic process
tasks.description: Read NIST SP 800-86 and summarize the four phases: collection, examination, analysis and reporting. Note the guidance on order of volatility and evidence integrity.
tasks.completion_criteria: A summary describing each phase and listing data sources in order of volatility.

tasks.title: Create and verify a forensic image
tasks.description: Image a small USB stick or virtual disk you own using dd or FTK Imager, hash both source and image with SHA-256, and fill out a simple chain of custody form.
tasks.completion_criteria: Matching source and image hashes recorded alongside a completed chain of custody entry.

tasks.title: Analyze a disk image with Autopsy
tasks.description: Load a practice disk image into Autopsy, review the file system timeline, recover deleted files, and inspect web history artifacts. Record findings with timestamps.
tasks.completion_criteria: A notes file listing at least five artifacts with their paths, timestamps and significance.

tasks.title: Write a full forensic investigation report
tasks.description: Complete a forensics challenge room or practice case in a lab environment, covering disk and memory evidence. Produce a professional report with scope, methodology, evidence hashes, timeline and conclusions.
tasks.completion_criteria: A report containing an evidence log with hashes, a reconstructed timeline of at least 10 events, and supported conclusions.
